title: Five and Ten: Numbers Worth Knowing Well
objective: 5 and 10 are useful landmark quantities — many other quantities can be understood in relation to how far they are from 5 or from 10.
studentQuestion: Is this number close to 5? Close to 10? How do you know?
newIdea: Benchmark quantities — the direct prerequisite for Unit 1.2's Make-5/Make-10 complement work.

teaching.setup: A ten-frame with several dots filled in (e.g. 7 filled).
teaching.see: How many are filled in? How many empty spaces are left?
teaching.break: Separate how many filled from how many empty within the same ten-frame.
teaching.build: State both: 7 filled, 3 empty — the empty spaces are the distance to 10.
teaching.transform: The same quantity (7), described as 7, or as 3 away from 10 — same value, benchmark-relative form.

check.prompt: Fill in the empty spaces and count all 10 to confirm 7 + 3 = 10.

examples.transfer: A quantity near 5 instead of 10 (e.g. 4 on a five-frame, 1 away from 5).

mastery.evidence: Given a ten-frame with 6-9 filled, correctly states the number of empty spaces without recounting them individually, twice.
